definition: To have sexual intercourse with someone.
notes: Also used as a noun; very common across US, UK, and Australian English.

definition: To have sexual intercourse with someone.
notes: More prevalent in US than UK; double meaning with the anatomical noun adds crude resonance.

definition: To have sexual intercourse; describes the physical thrusting motion.
notes: Evokes the physical motion of sex; also describes animals mating; sometimes used for humping objects non-sexually.

definition: To have sexual intercourse (British English, very commonly used).
notes: Primarily British English; internationally known partly via Austin Powers films; lower perceived vulgarity than American equivalents; also means a type of tobacco and a carpet texture.

definition: To have sexual intercourse with someone.
notes: Also used as a noun ('an easy lay'); relatively mild register; transitive construction implies sexual access to a partner.

definition: To have sexual intercourse with someone, implying conquest or dominance.
notes: Connotation of achievement and conquest; almost always male-subject construction; also extremely common in non-sexual achievement contexts ('nailed it'), creating plausible deniability.

definition: To have vigorous, aggressive sexual intercourse with someone.
notes: Strong aggressive and forceful connotation; emphasizes repeated hard thrusting; higher crude intensity than generic intercourse terms.

definition: To have penetrative sexual intercourse with someone aggressively.
notes: Tool/machine metaphor emphasizing mechanical penetration; similar crude level to pound but slightly less ubiquitous in everyday spoken slang.

definition: To have forceful sexual intercourse with someone; agricultural metaphor for penetration.
notes: US spelling; British variant is 'plough'; agricultural metaphor implying force and deep penetration; slightly less common than pound or drill in spoken slang.

definition: To have casual sexual intercourse with someone.
notes: AAVE-influenced; rose to mainstream via internet culture circa 2012–2018; the phrase 'smash or pass' (would you have sex with or reject this person) drove widespread adoption across demographics.

definition: To have sexual intercourse with someone.
notes: Often appears in the phrase 'I'd tap that'; lighter vulgarity than 'bang' or 'bone'; more common in spoken slang than written.

definition: To have sexual intercourse with someone, as in 'hit that'.
notes: AAVE-influenced; almost always in phrase form ('hit that', 'I'd hit it', 'hit it and quit it'); strongly context-dependent since 'hit' has many non-sexual meanings.

definition: To have sexual intercourse (idiomatic phrase).
notes: Popularized by early 1990s R&B; now dated but still understood by older millennials and Gen X; rarely used in 2026.

definition: To have sexual intercourse with someone (mild transitive euphemism).
notes: Context-dependent; 'I'd do her' / 'I did him'; cross-generational and universal; one of the least vulgar possible expressions for the act.

definition: To have sexual intercourse ('it' serving as a universal stand-in for sex).
notes: One of the most universally understood English sex euphemisms; safe to deploy in most contexts where explicit language is inappropriate; 'just do it' carries an unintentional double meaning.

definition: To begin sexual activity; to have sexual intercourse.
notes: Popularized by Marvin Gaye's 1973 'Let's Get It On'; enduring cross-generational usage; also used for enthusiastic engagement in non-sexual contexts.

definition: To have sexual intercourse (passive construction framing sex as received or achieved).
notes: Extremely common across all English dialects; passive voice implies sexual access was granted by a partner; heavily used in discussions of sexual frustration or success.

definition: To obtain sexual activity; to have casual sex.
notes: 'Some' as synecdoche for sexual activity; also used in military context meaning to engage in combat; frames sex as a commodity or resource to be obtained.

definition: To have a casual sexual encounter, typically without an ongoing relationship.
notes: Deliberately ambiguous; can mean anything from kissing to intercourse depending on context and speaker; the dominant millennial/Gen-Z term for casual sex in 2026; also has a wholly non-sexual meaning (to connect or link up).

definition: To succeed in obtaining sexual activity with someone.
notes: Frames sex as competitive achievement or athletic success; traditionally male-coded but gender-neutral in usage; also means obtaining drugs in slang.

definition: To bring someone to bed for sexual intercourse; to have sex with.
notes: Somewhat literary register; more common in written fiction and journalism than spoken slang; 'he bedded her' implies seduction leading to sex.

definition: To have sexual intercourse with someone (polite euphemism).
notes: One of the most universally acceptable English euphemisms; used in news reporting and polite conversation; technically absurd (literal sleep can occur non-sexually) but universally understood.

definition: To have sexual intercourse (British English, mildly crude).
notes: Primarily British; lighter and more playful tone than 'shag'; frequent in 1990s tabloid press; also means to hit someone on the head.

definition: To have sexual intercourse (Australian English, crude).
notes: Almost exclusively Australian English; considered highly vulgar in AU context; largely unrecognized as a sexual term in other English dialects; low global recognition reflects regional restriction.

definition: To have sexual intercourse with someone (British slang, now largely dated).
notes: British English; primarily mid-20th-century usage; largely supplanted by other terms; creates unintentional humor due to conflict with military/aviation communication term meaning 'message received'; also a common given name.
